title: Code Editions and Building Life Explorer
description: Calculate how many code editions are published during a building's service life and how many times each building component is replaced, given the building's life and each component's life.
creator: The Science of the Built Environment
author: Dan McCreary
subject: The Science of the Built Environment
chapter_title: Appendix H: Energy Codes and Building Performance Standards

pedagogical.learningObjective: Calculate how many code editions are published during a building's service life and how many times each building component is replaced, given the building's life and each component's life.
recommendedUsage: Read challenge 1 and type a whole number of code editions. Press Check.
After each answer the timeline fills in the part that the challenge asks about.
When the slider unlocks, change the building life from 30 to 100 years and watch the editions and the replacement counts update.
Find the components that stay for the whole life at 60 years, then raise the life to 100 years.
activities: Count (10 min): For building lives of 40, 60, and 90 years, count the editions and the replacements of each component by hand, then check with the sim.
What cannot be upgraded (10 min): List the parts that stay for the whole life at 60 years and explain why this argues for building them better than the current minimum.
Design a life (5 min): Choose a life for a school and justify it by the replacements it implies.
assessment: Students state the number of times a 30-year window is replaced in a 75-year life, with the arithmetic.
Students explain why the structural frame and the insulation and air barrier deserve more than the current code minimum.
